1.explanation: The core of this issue lies in the DataFilters component in DataFilters.js, which currently only supports a "drop" boolean prop and renders a DropButton for filter selection. To support a separate overlay, a new "layer" prop must be introduced and handled alongside or instead of the "drop" prop. The function DataFilters needs to accept and branch on the new prop to render a Grommet <Layer> wrapping the filter content. Corresponding TypeScript definitions in index.d.ts and PropTypes in propTypes.js must be updated to declare the new "layer" prop. These three files constitute the key elements to modify in order to add the requested layer functionality.
1.bug_scenario: When using <DataFilters drop /> with many filter controls, the dropdown overflows the viewport and provides no scrollable area. The desired behavior is to optionally render the filters in a full-screen Layer (modal) so that all filter fields can be seen and scrolled, instead of the limited DropButton dropdown.

2.explanation: The core of the issue lives in DataFilters.js, which currently only supports a `drop` boolean to render filters inside a DropButton. To implement the requested `layer` prop, DataFilters.js must be extended to accept and act on `layer`, rendering its content inside a Grommet Layer when `layer` is true. Alongside that change, prop type validation in propTypes.js and the TypeScript interface in index.d.ts need to include the new `layer` property so that consumers and type checkers recognize and enforce it. Updating these elements will allow DataFilters to switch between Drop and Layer rendering modes, preventing overflow when many filters are present.
2.bug_scenario: The DataFilters component’s dropdown (DropButton) is being used to display many filter controls, causing the dropContent to overflow the viewport and cut off scrollbars. The desired behavior is to provide a new `layer` prop on DataFilters so that, when enabled, the filters render inside a full‐screen or centered Layer overlay (rather than a constrained Drop), giving ample space without overflow.
